segment.description: Sulfur Fork Creek (USGS/TDEC spelling 'Sulphur Fork'), Robertson County, Tennessee (catalog) — a Red River tributary flowing through Springfield, Tennessee. This is the Red River-drainage creek in Robertson County, not any same-named water elsewhere; identity verified by HUC 05130206 and Robertson County (county code 147) on USGS/TDEC station metadata. TWRA's winter-trout site string is simply 'Sulphur Fork Creek' (Robertson) in the 2026 workbook; local reporting places the stocking along the Springfield Greenway, but that site detail is not from an agency source.
segment.boundaries: The named creek in Robertson County from the Springfield area down to the Red River confluence near Port Royal (TDEC stations span river-mile 0.1 at Port Royal Rd to mile 23.2-23.3 at the Springfield STP); USGS-03435770 'Sulphur Fk Red R above Springfield, TN' (65.6 sq mi drainage, alt 538.17 ft NGVD29).

coldSource.notes: Elevation is the USGS station altitude above Springfield. Identity verified from WQP station metadata columns (USGS station names 'SULPHUR FORK RED RIVER ...' and TDECWPC 'SULPHUR FORK'/'Sulphur FK CK' stations, all HUC 05130206, Robertson County) because the USGS identity endpoint has been 503ing this week. No cold-water source, spring, or canopy documentation found; the monitoring record (Springfield STP stations on the creek) indicates a developed-edge warmwater creek.

holdover.detail: No holdover documentation found. The TWRA program is winter-only catchable rainbows: 2026 workbook rows 'Sulphur Fork Creek' (Robertson, type Winter): 02/04/2026, 02/26/2026, TBD 12/2026, Rainbow Trout; the live TWRA schedule page contains the site string. No source documents survival between stockings or through summer.

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout documentation. TWRA's Trout Management Plan 2017-2027 places Tennessee's wild trout in East Tennessee streams and describes hatchery-supported waters as 'primarily warmwater habitats that cannot support trout year round' (canon quote; PDF not fetched per rule).

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: TDEC/USGS grab record shows 25-28.4 deg C summer water on Sulphur Fork (1980-2009) and the trout fishery is a winter-only catchable-rainbow program with no survival documentation.
